source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
New Jersey has 48 mapped data centers but only five publish power capacity, and CyrusOne's Totowa campus, at 6 MW, ranks fourth among them.

The gap between mapped and measured is the pattern. The five disclosed facilities total 111.3 MW, and NYM2 accounts for 5.4 percent of that. Its 200,000 square feet of technical space against 6 MW works out to roughly 30 watts per square foot, which is low density for AI workloads. At the 40 kW per rack typical of AI training, 6 MW supports about 150 racks. That is a regional colocation footprint, not a training campus, and the operator's specification does not break the load down by workload or accelerator type.

For AI specifically, the question the data cannot answer is whether 6 MW is a grid limit or a design choice. The record carries no power distribution architecture, no cooling capacity, and no interconnection detail, so there is no way to tell whether northern New Jersey headroom or the building itself caps this site. SSAE 16 Type II certification speaks to security and availability controls, not to compute. The suitability score of 52 rests only on published IT capacity and operator type, with announced expansion the one input flagged as missing.

What the record does not cover matters as much as what it does. There is no address and no usable coordinates, no accelerator inventory, and no workload split. The state figure of 111.3 MW is a floor set by disclosure rather than a measurement of what is built, because 43 of the 48 mapped facilities publish nothing at all. Any claim about New Jersey's AI capacity is therefore a claim about five buildings that chose to report, and NYM2 is one of them.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
